claims.text: High configurational entropy enhances the high-temperature structural and chemical stability of near-equiatomic HEA nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy or multi-element mixing increases lattice distortion in HEA nanoparticles.
Increased lattice distortion raises diffusion barriers and slows atomic diffusion.
Sluggish atomic diffusion restricts atom mobility and suppresses phase separation.
Sluggish atomic diffusion preserves uniform elemental distributions and suppresses elemental segregation during annealing.
Near-equiatomic nanoparticles are more stable than otherwise similar nanoparticles with slightly shifted compositions.
Multi-element mixing thermodynamically favors an alloyed structure through increased mixing entropy.
A slight deviation from equiatomic ratios produces meaningfully lower configurational entropy.
Slightly off-equiatomic nanoparticles have less lattice distortion than near-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Slightly off-equiatomic nanoparticles diffuse more rapidly than near-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Slightly off-equiatomic nanoparticles are consequently more prone to elemental segregation and phase changes.
After identical high-temperature exposure, near-equiatomic nanoparticles will retain a more uniform single-phase structure than slightly off-equiatomic nanoparticles.
Entropy-stabilized multi-element nanoparticles can retain a uniform elemental distribution during simulated annealing at 773 K.
Rapid synthesis locks nanoparticles into a high-entropy, homogeneous single-phase state.
The proposed entropy-stabilization mechanism applies throughout catalytic temperatures of 773–1173 K and thermoelectric temperatures of 473–1923 K.
Support interactions and specific elemental combinations can modulate high-temperature nanoparticle stability.
Using similar substrates for both composition groups helps control stability differences caused by nanoparticle anchoring and support interactions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and baseline describe the comparator as 'off-eutectic,' whereas the other fields describe it as 'off-equiatomic.' Eutectic and equiatomic compositions are distinct concepts, so the intended comparator is inconsistent.
